title: Autoclaving Erlenmeyer Flasks for Sterile Algal Cultures
author: Jakub Nedbal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bd2di8a6
materials: Prepare all the autoclave equipment as listed in the Materials section above. Autoclave parts and a sturdy lab jack laid out on a tidy lab bench.
Plug the Countdown Timer into a mains socket.

steps.title: Prepare cleaning area
steps.instruction: Wipe the dish‑washing area with 70 % denatured ethanol and ensure the surface is clean before starting.

steps.title: Remove permanent marker from flasks
steps.instruction: Wash away all permanent‑marker labels and writing from each Erlenmeyer flask using 70 % denatured ethanol.

steps.title: Wash flasks with detergent
steps.instruction: Scrub the inside of each used flask with dish‑washing liquid using a vial‑cleaning brush to remove dried algae and other residues.

steps.title: Rinse flasks with hot and cold water
steps.instruction: Rinse many times with copious amounts of hot and cold water to remove all detergent; fill each flask with hot water and empty it at least 10 times, then repeat with cold water.

steps.title: Final deionized water rinse
steps.instruction: Pour a dash of deionized water into each flask, swish it around the entire interior, then empty by abruptly turning the flask upside down; repeat if possible to improve rinsing, especially in hard‑water areas.

steps.title: Dry flasks
steps.instruction: Place the rinsed flasks on a wall‑mounted drying rack and allow them to dry completely.

steps.title: Seal flasks with cotton
steps.instruction: Once completely dry, plug each flask mouth with a clean cotton‑wool roll or ball.

steps.title: Prepare aluminium foil seals
steps.instruction: Cut a ~10 cm × 10 cm (4" × 4") piece of aluminium foil for each flask; if the foil is thinner than 24 µm, make the piece larger and fold it to create two‑ or three‑ply thickness.

steps.title: Wrap flasks with foil and tape
steps.instruction: Gently wrap the aluminium foil over the cotton wool plug—neither too tight nor too loose—and stick a small piece of autoclave tape on top of the foil without tightening the foil.

steps.title: Set up autoclave workspace
steps.instruction: Clear a solid desk, place a strong lab jack or other heat‑resistant support away from the desk edge, and keep the area tidy.

steps.title: Add water to autoclave
steps.instruction: Pour hot tap water into the autoclave up to 1 cm (½") below the heating‑spiral seal, ensuring no water reaches the external electrical connector; cold tap water may be used but will lengthen the cycle.

steps.title: Place autoclave on support
steps.instruction: Position the autoclave on the heat‑resistant support prepared in the previous step.

steps.title: Load flasks into autoclave
steps.instruction: Insert the autoclaving container and load it with the prepared conical flasks (up to nine comfortably, never more than ten).

steps.title: Close autoclave lid
steps.instruction: Place the lid on the autoclave, align the fixing loops with the screws, and orient the pressure‑release valves so they point toward the wall, away from people.

steps.title: Secure lid with wing nuts
steps.instruction: Screw all five sealing wing nuts gently, then tighten them in small steps using a non‑adjacent sequence (e.g., A‑C‑E‑B‑D) and repeat until each nut is hand‑tight.

steps.title: Connect power and timer
steps.instruction: Plug the power‑supply lead into the autoclave (ensure all connections are dry), then plug the autoclave lead into the Countdown Timer.

steps.title: Set countdown timer
steps.instruction: Press the delay button on the Countdown Timer twice to set a ½‑hour (30 min) countdown; two blue lights indicate the timer is running.

steps.title: Start autoclave heating
steps.instruction: Turn on the mains switch; monitor the pressure gauge as the autoclave heats—approximately 15 min to reach operating temperature when starting with hot water (longer with cold water).

steps.title: Mark first pressure rise
steps.instruction: When the pressure reaches 0.18‑0.19 MPa, the safety valve will release steam; note this time and continue autoclaving for a total of 15‑20 min after this first pressure point.

steps.title: Perform ON‑OFF pressure cycles
steps.instruction: When pressure shows 0.18 MPa, turn the power OFF at the mains socket; wait until pressure drops to ≤0.15 MPa, then turn the power ON again. When pressure rises back to 0.18 MPa (≈45 s), turn the power OFF once more. Repeat these ON‑OFF cycles (5‑7 cycles) until 15‑20 min have elapsed since the first 0.18 MPa point or the timer shuts off.

steps.title: Final power off and cool
steps.instruction: After completing the cycles, switch off the power at the socket, unplug the Countdown Timer, and let the autoclave stand to cool and depressurize (ideally overnight); do not use the release valve for rapid cooling.

steps.title: Open cooled autoclave
steps.instruction: Once the autoclave has reached room temperature, loosen the lid nuts (use the supplied spanner if needed); if the lid is sealed by under‑pressure, pry it open with the spanner.

steps.title: Unload and dry autoclave
steps.instruction: Remove the lid and its contents, pour out any remaining water, and let the autoclave dry before storage; dry the lid stand upside down to allow trapped water to drain.
